CHOICES MADE. (1) The lookup widens describe_schema's existing node_type rather than adding an argument: the call an agent makes when it guesses "Lemma" is a type now answers instead of refusing, and no schema in tools/list grows. (2) find_tools counts a term as an exact name match counts, weighed by how rare it is on the surface, not lifted to the top, so a word with an everyday sense ranks by evidence. (3) An edge's terms ride the full listing and the lookup, not pair candidates: on all 784 pairs they pushed five X -> Contributor replies over budget and cut their hints from 800 to 240 characters. (4) PREMISE_OF and CONCLUDES have no typed helper, so an edge with none names the constructors of the one type it is pinned to (add_inference). (5) find_tools' description now says it searches a field's words: the one toolsnap that changes, because the list it gives grew.

JUDGED OUT, each held by the term-table test: "assumption" (req:assumptions-are-first-class keeps its type open), "given" (a participle in proofs, a preposition in the corpus, and its noun is "hypothesis"), "used in" (ordinary English), "combinatorial proof" (two meanings), bare "contradiction", "construction" and "double counting" (each names something else a design says; the methods are named "proof by ..."), and no term on DEPENDS_ON (functional need, not a premise) or DECOMPOSES (a case split is an inference whose exhaustiveness is a premise). "induction" stays bare although "induction motor" ranks add_inference first, because it is the SHOWN WHEN sentence's own word. Plurals ("lemmas") are left for later.
